messages:
maya: heads up — did a quick bring-up of the small reranker quant variant (int8-ish) on the core eval harness. overall rouge-ish numbers look okay but a couple of weird slices. sending raw notes.
liam: what weird slices?
maya: overall NDCG@10 down ~3.8% vs float baseline, MRR@10 nearly flat. but long-query bucket (>= 300 tokens) has NDCG down ~9%. short-faq queries (~<30 tokens) slightly up.
stef: hmm that pattern screams truncation/prefix cache differences or tokenizer mismatch. did you use the same tokenization pipeline as prod?
maya: used eval harness tokenizer (hf-tokenizer v2) and the model's compiled tokenization. I double-checked vocab parity but not the normalization step (we might be stripping HTML in prod only).
arjun: can you paste the eval command + config you ran?
maya: here:
```
python -m eval.run \
  --model rerank-small-int8 \
  --candidates 100 \
  --batch 64 \
  --dataset redwood-relevance-v2 \
  --split test \
  --tokenizer hf-v2 \
  --truncate_strategy suffix \
  --seed 42
```

nora: seed 42 — good. did you run multiple seeds? int8 tends to have non-deterministic kernel jitter.
maya: only 1 seed so far. rerunning with 5 seeds now. initial single-run outputs (summary):
```
NDCG@10: float=0.312, int8=0.300 (-3.8%)
MRR@10: float=0.184, int8=0.182 (-1.1%)
NDCG_long(>=300): float=0.278, int8=0.253 (-9.0%)
NDCG_short(<30): float=0.265, int8=0.271 (+2.3%)
```

eva: can you run with prefix caching disabled? small model kvpack differences sometimes penalize long contexts under quantization. also try truncation=prefix vs suffix.
liam: also test candidate ordering sensitivity: we saw earlier that different candidate shuffles change ndcg by ~1% for this dataset. ensure you use fixed candidate sorting (by score or by id).
maya: good call. current run used original candidate order. will re-run with sorted-by-score and sorted-by-id for parity.
stef: another quick check — for long docs, are we concatenating multiple passages per doc? if so, quantized attention math could change effective attention float rounding across chunk boundaries. try single-passage baseline.
arjun: how big is the eval sample per slice? small sample sizes inflate apparent deltas.
maya: test set long slice size ~1.2k queries, short slice ~800. but effective evaluated pairs ~120k candidates for long. I'll add bootstrap CI (1000 resamples) to check significance.
nora: if bootstrap CI overlaps, then might be noise. but 9% seems large. also run cross-dataset check: try redwood-relevance-v1 and a smaller curated dev set.
maya: agreed. also noticed top-1 hit rate drop for some query cohorts (software-qa) — might be tokenization of code blocks. will run with html_strip=True and codeblock-preserve=True to see impact.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered: rerank-small-int8-smoke (id: ci-78821). started at 3567890130.
eva: please add a quick diff of softmax logits distribution between float and int8 on a small sample (10 queries). if quantization causes logit compression, that could lower top-k separation.
maya: pasted sample logits diff for 1 query below (first 6 cand logits float -> int8):
```
float_logits: [2.34, 1.12, 0.92, 0.01, -0.55, -1.20]
int8_logits:  [2.10, 1.05, 0.80,  0.02, -0.60, -1.30]
```

liam: looks like slight compression at the top but order preserved. softmax temp sensitivity maybe. try scaling calibration (per-head or global gain) — we have an INT8-corrected rescale factor in runtime configs.
arjun: also run a ranker eval where we re-score float model outputs with the int8 model (i.e., use float candidate features but int8 scorer) — that'll isolate candidate generation vs scorer rounding.
maya: noted. plan summary: 1) run 5 seeds + bootstrap CI, 2) run with truncation prefix/suffix + single vs multi-passage, 3) force tokenizer normalizations (html strip, code handling), 4) evaluate sorted candidate orders, 5) collect logits distributions and try runtime rescale, 6) cross-dataset sanity (v1 and curated).
nora: timeline?
maya: results in ~3 hours for full matrix (CI running). will post artifacts. if we still see gap after all, escalate to quantization infra (stef + ops) to check kernel parity.
steF: (reacts :eyes:) — I'll stand by for kernel logs.
liam: assignable tasks?
maya: I'll own seeds + candidate ordering + tokenizer toggles. arjun will run single-vs-multipassage and bootstrap. nora will run cross-dataset. eva will produce logits diffs and try rescale. stef will monitor kernels if we have persistent gap.
eva: ack.
arjun: ack.
nora: ack.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline ci-78821 passed smoke tests at 3567890175. artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/rerank-small-int8/ci-78821/
maya: thx — pulling logs now. will report back with table of per-slice ndcg + CI. :memo:
